key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within minutes to hours. LOCATION: UNILATERAL flank pain, may radiate to groin. DURATION: Lasts hours to days. CHARACTER: SEVERE, SHARP, COLIC pain. AGGRAVATING: MOVEMENT, urination. RELIEVING: PAIN medications, hydration. TIMING: Sudden onset, lasts hours to days. SEVERITY: 8-10/10, severe and unrelenting. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: SEVERE FLANK PAIN, may have nausea, vomiting, hematuria, may have fever if infected. KEY POSITIVES: Severe flank pain, hematuria, positive imaging. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Severe pain with fever - possible infected stone, call 911
Signs of severe infection - fever, chills, rigors - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of severe metabolic acidosis - deep breathing, confusion, coma - call 911
Signs of severe electrolyte imbalances - confusion, seizures, cardiac arrhythmias - call 911
